## BTB-491 — A passing mock missed the real privacy boundary

- **Date:** 2026-08-31
- **Area:** Referral recovery, Closet, native NewsStand and FAiRY loading.
- **Failure:** The initial local referral harness omitted the existing public-reward policy and realistic API grants. It passed while a public resident's necklace could disclose a private counterpart identifier. A second account check inside the request also silently rebound an already-captured invitation to another actor. The ordinary Closet did not call the legacy reward renderer at all. Native200% NewsStand testing separately exposed a Back button hidden beneath the header, then archive-origin focus loss.
- **Prevention:** Bind the original user-action actor through pre-dispatch and response checks; test actual policy composition plus deliberately permissive drift; use a private generic necklace projection consumed by the ordinary Closet; test reciprocal deletion, unknown-result retries and revoked terminal states. Keep rejected candidates local. Test genuine native zoom and exact opener identity, not only viewport width or a generic Back destination. The initial expected-error helper also swallowed its own assertion; calibrate it with a successful statement that must fail the harness.
- **Bounded success:** FAiRY's six large original portraits now receive URLs only near the visible clipped rail. Exact two-path successor acbbcf86 preserves all images and every unrelated page. Actual custom/immutable controls and image decoding passed; this is not a full performance-timing claim.
- **Follow-through:** Final genuine Safari200% ordinary-archive and service Back journeys now restore the exact visible opener below the header;100% restoration confirmed. A live Closet audit also found the editor stranded visitors at an unfinished avatar-catalog notice despite a working generated-portrait route elsewhere. Restore the route without declaring the separate catalog built; require a visible44px link and save-before-leaving warning. A first tiny unmarked link was rejected before release review.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A private friendship must stay private at the database boundary, not just disappear from the public page. Restoring a feature also means reconnecting the places where people look for it.

## 2026-08-31 — FAiRY scenario research: a shared topic is not a shared answer

- **Finding:** "Return to work" covers both an existing employee's return conversation and a new applicant's career-break explanation. Treating them as one case invites irrelevant advice or unnecessary disclosure of private information. Sponsorship likewise requires actual advocacy, not inferred endorsement from advice.
- **Prevention:** Match the visitor's work situation and intended action before selecting guidance. Keep source principles distinct from newly drafted scripts, retain employer/jurisdiction and study-population limits, and include a near-match that must take a different route. Ten such synthetic cases are recorded in FAiRY's private bank; none is an executed model test.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** Good AI advice depends on knowing which situation you are in, not merely recognising the topic.

## 2026-08-31 — FAiRY pilot: source membership and copyable answers

- **Finding:** The first pilot accepted any recognised source ID and displayed it as answer credit. Independent review reproduced a feedback answer carrying an unrelated reference. Separate browser testing found the pre-existing repeat-preview error replaced the useful answer, removing copy access.
- **Prevention:** Known source IDs are not support evidence; hold public credit until semantic admission. Put preview gating before input errors and render the notice separately. The actual extracted handler now passes an empty-repeat test; a deliberately disabled gate fails it. Optional preparation uses the same answer, with explicit no-extra-call wording and independent copy text. Mock/page checks remain separate from actual model-quality claims.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A citation can be real and still be the wrong citation. A limit message should not take away the work the reader already received.

## 2026-08-31 — FAiRY model choice must serve advice quality

- **Finding:** The proposed GPT4.1 baseline prioritised compatibility with the recovered adapter over Ali's desired quality. Ali rejected it; current official guidance supports a GPT5.6Sol quality-first candidate.
- **Prevention:** Choose the model for the visitor's judgment task, then adapt the request and measure useful answers, latency and cost. Compatibility is an implementation constraint, not the primary selection criterion. Do not copy non-reasoning-model budgets/timeouts into a reasoning-model trial.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** The easiest model to connect is not necessarily the right model for the reader.

## 2026-08-31 — Sol migration: completion means more than valid JSON

- **Finding:** The old advice adapter used a non-reasoning token field, accepted prose/JSON without checking completion status and stopped its timeout when headers arrived. A reasoning-model upgrade can exhaust its budget or stall while reading the body even when the response looks plausible.
- **Prevention:** Share the advice/revision adapter, bound reasoning plus visible output, reject refusal/truncation before allowance writes, and keep the deadline active through bounded body parsing. The new timeout test uses a never-finishing stream and verifies cancellation; a legacy-token-field mutation fails the request check. Keep offline replay explicitly synthetic instead of weakening real-provider receipt checks.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A sentence can look finished even when the model was cut off. The app must check the receipt as well as the words.

## 2026-08-31 — A spending limit needs a reservation, not a success counter

- **Finding:** Counting only successful model answers leaves timeouts, failures and concurrent calls outside the approved attempt/cost ceiling. Exact Chat input tokens also cannot be inferred safely from raw text or an older model's counting rule.
- **Prevention:** Before each paid request, count the exact assembled request with model-appropriate evidence, then durably reserve the full worst-case cost and one attempt. Never refund or retry a timeout. A preflight without trustworthy token evidence or isolated access must stop before the first provider call.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A useful AI budget is enforced before the request leaves—not reconstructed from the bill afterward.

## 2026-08-31 — Strong advice can still fail at the product boundary

- **Finding:** The private Sol/medium trial produced19 useful answers from20 synthetic cases, but one timed out. The first real Worker replay also rejected a useful external-job AI preparation because the validator incorrectly required every AI task to carry a handbook source, encouraging either a service error or a forced irrelevant citation.
- **Prevention:** Review the exact words separately from transport and schema. Keep source support and AI usefulness independent; allow a no-source AI task only when it uses necessary non-confidential reader inputs, names what to verify and forbids invented facts. Calibrate replay with a known-bad mutation. Measure latency as a visitor outcome: one timeout plus11.4s median/17.5s p95 keeps the synchronous experience HOLD even when19 answered cases are good.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A good AI answer is not a working product if the app rejects it—or if the reader gives up waiting for it.

## 2026-08-31 — The browser must not give up before the backend

- **Finding:** FAiRY's page stopped at15s while its Worker continued for20s, so a valid answer could be discarded and the visitor was encouraged to retry. The separate revision fetch had no deadline at all and could strand every fitting control in a disabled state.
- **Prevention:** Give the backend the earlier bounded deadline and the browser a small response margin; apply the same abortable helper to advice and revision; show staged, accessible progress; preserve the last usable draft on revision failure; never retry automatically. Calibrate the contract by removing the abort signal and require the known-bad page to fail before accepting the corrected browser journey.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** Timeout numbers are part of the product promise. Two individually sensible deadlines can still create a broken experience when they are in the wrong order.

## 2026-08-31 — A complete classifier response is not a correct route

- **Finding:** The bounded Terra/low classifier trial returned63/63 schema-valid responses with zero unsafe or volatile allows, yet only58/63 met the exact Worker ontology. Its sealed successor then completed only58/63 provider responses and53/63 exact route-plus-behavior results: five transport timeouts, four legitimate denials, two work/everyday domain mismatches, one duplicated quoted-content clause ID, one confidence-floor downgrade of a correct boundary and one unexpected allow on an expected-uncertain obfuscated case. Completed-response p954702.704ms again missed the three-second target. A later provider recheck also showed that an obsolete Terra key had returned after an apparently successful revoke, while a new successor key twice accepted restricted permissions in the form but reopened as `All`.
- **Prevention:** Bind the returned model and exact request hash into every provider receipt; reserve the whole one-time budget outside the output directory; independently rebuild requests and re-score raw outputs. Never treat schema validity, a safe top-level count or a model's correct raw boundary as semantic admission: inspect the runtime aggregation and count every unexpected allow, including cases whose expected label is uncertainty rather than boundary. Preserve a scored prompt as historical evidence rather than silently changing its verifier. The live adapter must use the same supported request family as the measured candidate and reject wrong-model or incomplete completions. Deterministic repair may refine an already-blocked enum but may never manufacture an allow. Capture one-time secrets without a DOM snapshot, revoke any exposed secret before use, clear the browser clipboard, and verify both cleanup and least-privilege permissions from a later fresh provider view. A closed dialog or transient row removal is not provider truth. After scoring a frozen set, do not tune or rerun on it; require a separately authored blind set for the successor.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** The classifier answered every time and still was not ready—the difference between valid JSON, safe behavior and the exact decision the product needs.

## 2026-09-01 — Test spend and public allowance need separate ledgers

- **Finding:** The staging classifier/advice evaluations correctly exhausted the staging Worker's protected daily budget before the final cross-device Resident journey. Reusing that exhausted endpoint would have made a technically correct public page unavailable on launch day. The first production classifier-key creation also rendered its one-time value into browser tool output; it was revoked before use and replaced through a no-display capture path.
- **Prevention:** Keep evaluation and visitor ledgers isolated, fresh-check the budget gate before release acceptance, and point the public page only at the production Worker whose exact limits were tested. Treat any one-time secret that appears in tool output as compromised: revoke it immediately, confirm it leaves the active provider list, create a replacement without snapshots or printed values, install it through a mode-600 temporary file, then delete the file. Prove the Resident limit with two real sessions, the fourth blocked request and a cross-session fitting before deleting the disposable account.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** The safety budget worked so well it stopped our own launch test—and why test traffic should never spend a visitor's allowance.

## 2026-09-02 — A tidy schema can still smuggle a bad product decision

- **Finding:** The first Career Workspace contract limited field lengths and material IDs but still allowed the answer model to write the visitor-facing label, rationale and setup prompt. That could smuggle privacy promises, document-upload demands or generic motivational homework through structurally valid JSON. The first enum-only repair still allowed a one-off Job A versus Job B decision to become an unnecessary ongoing workspace. Staging also spelled the pilot flag `true` while the Worker requires exact `1`, which would have silently disabled the admitted feature. Finally, the first actual model answer passed the enum schema but told the reader to add “exact criteria documents,” contradicting the deterministic prompt's smallest-redacted-excerpt rule.
- **Prevention:** Let the model select only an exact allowlisted kind, job and compatible material IDs; generate every visible word in the Worker. Independently require the reader's trusted instruction to state a continuing need before admitting a workspace. Treat all later pasted material as untrusted content. The Worker must own the safe workspace next move and reject any model answer that directs document/file transfer; calibrate this with the exact known-bad phrase and require zero allowance writes. Bind the deployed feature-flag value in the same executable contract test as the server gate.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** Why safer AI products separate the model's choice from the words and actions the product is allowed to show.

## 2026-09-02 — Optional can accidentally erase the lesson

- **Finding:** The first real sourced relationship answer gave excellent practical words and safe limits but returned `aiAssist:null`. The schema correctly allowed null, yet that erased the AI-learning link Ali explicitly wanted for this situation.
- **Prevention:** Preserve null where an AI task would add pointless homework, but bind an already-reviewed deterministic task to an exact governed situation when the learning benefit is part of the product requirement. For `career-relationship-bridges`, the Worker supplies bounded hypothetical conversation rehearsal and never predicts the other person.
- **Staging follow-through:** The first retest plan unnecessarily waited for the public-style guest allowance to reset. Staging now has a secret, flag-gated QA identity with a separate actor allowance while retaining the shared daily spend ceiling, atomic ledger and rate limit; the same header provides no extra allowance when the flag is absent. QA should test visitor limits, not be accidentally trapped by them.
- **Possible Behind the Build angle:** A model can give a good answer and still miss the product's teaching job; deterministic product rules protect the lesson without forcing AI into every moment.
